editorial:
Imagine finding out you have a daughter you never knew about, only for her to tell you to get lost. That is exactly what happens to the retired Hofrat Geiger. He is a bit stiff, but he truly wants to help his daughter, who owns a crumbling inn that is basically falling apart. The vibe here is a classic, cozy comedy of errors. You will love seeing the awkward tension as they try to figure out their relationship, especially when she agrees to a fake marriage just to get her citizenship papers sorted out. It is a sweet, lighthearted story about family and second chances.

What really makes this work is the funny way Geiger plays a long game, delaying her paperwork just to keep her around while he secretly fixes up her inn. The pacing is steady, and the acting feels very natural for the era. While it is an older film, the charm is timeless. It is a perfect pick if you want something heartwarming and low-stress.
endingExplained: In the end, the fake marriage turns into something real. The daughter finally realizes that Geiger actually loves her and has been helping her all along by renovating her inn in secret. The tension disappears when she discovers his kind heart. They drop the act and decide to be a real family. The movie wraps up with the inn looking great and the two of them finally finding peace and happiness together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old-school family comedies and heartwarming stories.
